0.title: Break the doomscroll.
0.sub: YouTube Tweak disables YouTube's infinite scroll and hands you one honest red button — so the feed stops when you tell it to, not when the algorithm decides you've had enough.

1.title: See when it really posted.
1.sub: Turn YouTube’s vague “5 months ago” into the exact publish date, shown on every video — so you always know how old it really is.

2.title: Find it in a keystroke.
2.sub: A command-style quick search jumps to any video, channel, or setting — without ever leaving the page you’re on.

3.title: Hide what you don’t want.
3.sub: One click removes any video — clickbait, Shorts, channels you’re done with — and keeps it gone for good.

mock.caption: Infinite scroll disabled — you click to continue.

problem.title: Infinite scroll isn't a convenience. It's a trap you didn't opt into.

stats.title: The feed never ends
stats.body: Every video auto-loads the next batch. There's no bottom, so there's no natural moment to stop.

stats.title: "Just one more" adds up
stats.body: A quick check turns into a lost evening. The design rewards staying, not leaving.

stats.title: Decisions you actually made
stats.body: You never chose to keep scrolling — the page just kept feeding. Attention on autopilot.

how.title: One switch: the endless feed becomes a single button.

items.title: Reclaim your hours
items.body: Stop losing evenings to a feed engineered to never end. Watch what you came for, then leave.

items.title: You're in control
items.body: The next batch loads only when you click the button. Every step forward is a choice.

items.title: Same YouTube, calmer
items.body: Nothing else changes — search, playback, subscriptions all work. The endless scroll just stops.

install.title: Take back the scroll today.
install.sub: Free, open source, and it works the moment you install it. No account, no setup.

problem.title: “5 months ago” hides the one thing you need — the actual date.

items.title: Timestamps keep drifting
items.body: The same upload reads “2 days ago,” then “3 weeks ago,” then “5 months ago.” The number never stops moving.

items.title: The year disappears
items.body: Relative time hides whether a tutorial is from this month or five years ago — exactly what you need to judge it.

items.title: Impossible to compare
items.body: Two videos both say “last year.” Which came first? Relative dates simply won’t tell you.

how.title: One popup. Every date, exactly your way.
how.body: Open the extension popup and shape the timestamp however you read it best — the change lands on every video instantly.

points.title: Gregorian or Hijri
points.body: Pick the calendar you actually think in.

points.title: Every field, your style
points.body: Weekday, day, month and year — long, short, narrow, numeric, 2-digit, or off.

points.title: Live bilingual preview
points.body: See the result in Arabic and English before you save.

items.title: Absolute timestamps
items.body: See the exact publish date on every video instead of a vague “x ago.”

items.title: Your format, your rules
items.body: Pick weekday, day, month and year styles — long, short, numeric, 2-digit, or hidden.

items.title: Hijri & Gregorian
items.body: Switch calendars in one tap — 16 Ramadan 1447 AH or 5 January 2026.

items.title: Bilingual preview
items.body: Watch the date update live in Arabic and English as you tweak it.

install.title: See every date as it really is.
install.sub: Available now. Free and open source — set your format once and every video shows its true date.

problem.title: Every search starts by leaving what you're watching.

items.title: You lose your place
items.body: Opening youtube.com to search means abandoning the page — or video — you were already on.

items.title: The same steps, every time
items.body: New tab, load YouTube, click the box, then finally type. Four moves for one search.

items.title: The feed grabs you first
items.body: You meant to search one thing — but the home feed pulls you in before you get the chance.

how.title: Hit Enter. You're on the results.
how.body: Open the popup from any page and start typing. Real YouTube suggestions appear instantly — pick one and land straight on the results.

points.title: Live YouTube suggestions
points.body: Real autocomplete as you type, in your language.

points.title: Keyboard-first
points.body: ⌘/Ctrl + 1–9 to open a result, arrows to move, Enter to go.

points.title: Searches your selection
points.body: Highlight text on any page — the box opens pre-filled, ready to search.

items.title: Search from anywhere
items.body: Reach YouTube search from any tab — no need to open the site first.

items.title: Live suggestions
items.body: Real YouTube autocomplete, in English and Arabic, the moment you type.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts
items.body: ⌘/Ctrl + a number opens that result instantly; arrows and Enter do the rest.

items.title: Right-click to search
items.body: Select text anywhere and pick “Search on YouTube” — results open in a new tab, keeping your place.

install.title: Search YouTube without opening YouTube.
install.sub: Available now. Free and open source — one keystroke to any video, from wherever you are.
